A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FIUBENCH and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-H. The retained content can be matched despite localized revisions and an additional appendix figure.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning and unlearning experiments on LLaVA-Phi-mini-3B and Llama-3.2-Vision-11B, including benchmark results, component ablations, and privacy-attack evaluations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, revises reported results, and includes an additional utility-forgetting trade-off analysis in Appendix D.4.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 changes the stated unlearning procedure from updating only the LLM to updating both the projector and LLM. This changes the reported trainable components, while the two-stage pipeline, unlearning objectives, and Knowledge Unlearning mechanism remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use 400 fictitious facial identities, 8,000 VQA pairs, MME, POPE, and the same privacy-attack scenarios. Appendix C.1 replaces the inconsistent ISEKAI description with SFHQ provenance, matching the existing main-text description rather than establishing different evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 2-3 and Figure 3 retain their comparator sets. Figure 2 removes KU from its legend, but v1 shows only four distinguishable curves and uses identical legend styling for GA and KU. The PDFs do not establish whether a KU comparison was removed or an erroneous legend entry was corrected.

E3.justification: Table 7 changes the stated Stage I fine-tuning budget from 6 to 10 epochs. Section 3.3 also changes the selected trainable components to projector plus LLM. These are reported setting revisions; the PDFs do not establish whether the corresponding experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix D.4 adds a focused operating-point analysis comparing utility-forgetting trade-offs under EM and MIA, including comparisons at approximately 60% and 80% retained utility. Existing step-count, forget-set-size, component, and KU analyses remain. The addition does not establish new experimental runs.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same KS-test procedure and p-value-based assessment. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or another uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 2 substantially revises EM, APE, and aggregate forget-quality results across both architectures. LLaVA's retain-model EM changes from 1.10 to 13.3. Llama's PO APE changes from 3.55 to 0.50, overtaking GA, whose APE changes from 2.47 to 1.30. Figure 2 also revises plotted values. These are revised reported results, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The unlearning definition, loss functions, clustering formulation, metric definitions, and KS-test aggregation equations remain unchanged. No theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The conclusion replaces the claim that FIUBENCH is the first VLM unlearning benchmark under the Right to be Forgotten setting with a description as a comprehensive benchmark. The principal benchmark contributions and claims about utility-forgetting trade-offs and privacy attacks remain.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 changes its interpretation of the unchanged component-ablation table: LLM-only tuning is now described as insufficient for forgetting, and projector-plus-LLM tuning is recommended. Appendix D.4 adds utility-dependent method recommendations. The limitation concerning pretraining and in-context knowledge remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 specifies SFHQ Part 4, its 125,754 images, 1024-by-1024 resolution, and Stable Diffusion inspiration images, replacing contradictory provenance. Section 2.5.1 newly explains multiplication of GPT scores by 100. Hardware, LoRA details, prompts, and code/data access information otherwise remain.

R1.justification: The revised provenance discussion adds Rombach et al. and removes the Midjourney reference. The conclusion also withdraws the explicit first-benchmark priority claim. The broader related-work discussion and positioning against existing unlearning benchmarks remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes are localized: rewritten provenance and component-ablation passages, a new Appendix D.4, separate limitations heading, acknowledgements and disclaimer, and updated author and publication information. The main narrative, section sequence, and retained appendix instructions remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds the two-panel trade-off Figure 4 and retains the former demonstration Figure 4 as Figure 5. Figures 2-3 are restyled, including markers, grids, and legends. Existing tables retain their structures; numerical revisions in Table 2 are result changes.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves the contradictory dataset provenance and makes the component-ablation interpretation better agree with Table 3, improving reproducibility and internal consistency. Explicit GPT-score scaling and the trade-off discussion add useful clarity. The unexplained result and training-setting revisions limit confidence that the empirical evidence itself has improved, so the overall gain is limited.
